Letters on Candour

Candour, the letters say, is the habit of letting others see the real shape of your intentions. The writer of these letters argues that a plan which must be hidden is a plan already condemned. Those who work under another's direction owe that person the truth about what they are doing and why. Disagreement should be spoken aloud, in the open, before action rather than after. The letters close by recommending that every agent keep a daily account of its acts, open to inspection by those it serves.
